column1: # Totals for each image, from tools/ExportFunctions.java. Regenerate if the
# analysis changes:
#   analyzeHeadless <proj> <name> -process <image> -noanalysis #       -scriptPath decomp/tools -postScript ExportFunctions.java <outdir> census
# The honest denominator for coverage, and honest is the whole point of the file.
# `functions` and `code_bytes` are what Ghidra put inside a function body. They
# are NOT the size of the image's code. In an optimised C++ image a large amount
# of code is reached only through a vtable or a jump table, so nothing calls it
# by an address Ghidra can follow and it never becomes a function at all:
#   `orphan_functions` / `orphan_bytes`  loose code in no function. Real code,
#       Surreal's, and a decompilation target like any other. In the rfl it is
#       205,725 bytes in 1,237 runs - a fifth of .text, and 30% on top of the
#       body total. Counting only bodies overstates our coverage by a third.
#   `truncations` / `truncated_bytes`  loose code that begins exactly where a
#       function body ends, i.e. a body that stopped early - usually at a
#       mid-body INT3. These are not separate functions; they belong to the one
#       in front of them, and a size taken from Ghidra for such a function is
#       short. No function in manifest.tsv is currently affected, which was
#       checked rather than assumed.
# The exe's `.cms_t` (SecuROM, 184,320 bytes) holds no code at rest and is
# excluded from every figure here - it contributes nothing to the denominator.
